claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the basics: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 20 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 20 years old, I need to ask some additional questions as Child Benefit eligibility for children over 16 depends on specific circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he enrolled in full-time non-advanced education such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school a while back and isn't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to make sure I have a complete picture of Alex's situation.

**Is Alex registered with a careers service or with Connexions (or equivalent youth support service), and has he left education or training within the last 20 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not registered with any careers service or anything like that. He left school more than 20 weeks ago now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just to make sure I have all the relevant details:

**Does Alex have any disabilities or health conditions that affect his ability to work or live independently?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't have any disabilities or health conditions that affect him in that way.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Child Benefit generally stops when a child turns 16, unless they continue in approved full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels) or approved training. In those cases, Child Benefit can continue until they turn 20. Since Alex is 20 years old and is not currently in any education or training program, he doesn't meet the qualifying criteria for Child Benefit.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he enrolls in approved education or training before he turns 20 - you may want to reconsider, though given his age, the window for this would be very limited.

If you have any other questions or if there's anything else I can help with, please let me know.
